subject: Onramp: traffic tracework, signoff checklist & owner mop-list
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@cyphertech.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@cyphertech.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onramp: traffic tracework, signoff checklist & owner mop-list

Hi Marta / Tom — great conversation this morning, thanks for walking through the high-level goals. Per our ask list, I pulled together a concise next-steps checklist so we can kick off the POC traffic intake without ambiguity. Rafael / Dev / Karthik copied for owner alignment.

Summary of call in one line: CypherTech wants a 2-week POC to validate 95th-percentile latency at production-like burst patterns for customer-facing summarization API.

Key asks (please fill the attached CSV template):
- Representative traffic trace export: 7 days of request logs (timestamp, endpoint, avg tokens in/out, user-agent) or a synthetic trace describing distribution.
- RPS profile: steady-state RPS and peak-burst RPS (per-minute granularity if possible).
- Token length distributions: histogram or percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for prompt tokens and generated tokens.
- Concurrency targets: typical concurrent sessions and worst-case concurrency during business hours.
- Failure/circuit cases: any known spike patterns (cron jobs, batch jobs, nightly reports).

Success criteria (draft — please confirm):
1) P95 latency for generation <= 350ms for L100 (100-token gen) under steady-state RPS;
2) P99 tail under burst (3x baseline) within 1.5s for L100;
3) Throughput hit-rate >= 99% (no throttling) for baseline SLA;
4) Cost per 1k tokens <= target in SOW (we'll refine after initial runs).

Owner/roles — Rafael will lead runtime mapping and model variant selection; Dev will run the ingestion and synthetic replay; Karthik will coordinate the quantization/instance sizing recommendations. Marta / Tom to provide the trace + signoff on success criteria by EOD next Wednesday (2027-08-04).

Attachments: ctech_onramp_workload_template.csv (fill and return), poc-success-metrics-v1.md (editable criteria).

Next steps:
1) Marta/Tom upload trace or completed CSV by 2027-08-04.
2) Dev to confirm replay environment and estimated test window (we expect 48-72h of true-run data collection).
3) Rafael to propose model/quantization pairs for two runs (latency-first and cost-first).
4) Karthik to deliver recommended instance mix prior to first run.

If anything here is off, call it out now — otherwise we will treat these as the working plan and start booking test windows.

Best,
Olga
---
Olga Petrov | Senior AE, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
Redwood Inference
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@cyphertech.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@cyphertech.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onramp: traffic tracework, signoff checklist & owner mop-list

Thanks Olga — this is clear and clean. Quick answers inline:
- We can export 10 days of request logs; I'll have our infra team scrub PII and share a CSV. Expect delivery by COB Tues 2027-08-03 (slightly earlier than your requested date).
- Baseline RPS: 12 RPS steady-state; typical business-hour concurrency 60 sessions; expected peak bursts ~45 RPS sustained over 3–5 minutes when product launches happen.
- Token distribution: p50 prompt 45 tokens, p95 prompt 220 tokens; generated tokens p50 80, p95 360.
- Nightly batch spikes: we have an ingestion job at 02:15 UTC that introduces ~30% traffic surge for 6 minutes.

We agree with the draft success criteria except the P95 steady-state latency target — our internal goal is 300ms if possible. I'll mark that as preferred; okay for Redwood to validate at 350ms with a stretch goal of 300ms.

We'll upload the scrubbed CSV and a short readme from infra describing log schema. Also attaching a one-pager on our major release cadence (to help schedule bursts).

— Marta
Marta Lopez | Head of Platform Engineering, CypherTech
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@cyphertech.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 12:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onramp: traffic tracework, signoff checklist & owner mop-list

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Marta — that token profile is super helpful. A few technical clarifications before we start replaying: 

1) Can you include a sample of raw payload size (bytes) per request and the model endpoint name (if you have multiple)? That helps us tune batch sizes and kernel selection.
2) For bursts: when you say ~45 RPS over 3–5 mins, is that typically all from a single endpoint or fanout across 3 endpoints?
3) Any auth rate-limiting on your side that we should mimic?

Preliminary plan from our side:
- Run two baseline replays: (A) steady-state 12 RPS for 3 hours; (B) burst ramp to 45 RPS for five 5-minute windows spaced across a 3-hour run. Collect p50/p95/p99 latency buckets, token/sec throughput, and model-serving queue depth.
- Run two config passes: latency-optimized (smaller batch, priority routing) and cost-optimized (bigger batch, lower priority).

Dev, please confirm we can allocate a replay window next Tue 2027-08-09 morning PT and reserve ~8h infra for data collection. Karthik, start sizing suggestions and list the quantization variants we intend to try.

Rafael
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@cyphertech.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onramp: traffic tracework, signoff checklist & owner mop-list

All, confirmed on Redwood side — I reserved the replay cluster for Tue 2027-08-10 08:00–18:00 PT (pushing to Wed morning if needed). Action items: 
- Marta: upload scrubbed CSV + sample payloads by 2027-08-03. We need the endpoint name column and bytes/request.
- Marta: confirm whether bursts are single-endpoint or multi-endpoint (short answer OK).
- Karthik: please post recommended instance mix and the two quantization options into the shared Drive folder by Mon 2027-08-08 EOD.
- Rafael: bring the test run dashboard template (latency/token metrics) for the kickoff.

I'll also attach a short runbook to the Drive folder that describes how we perform the replay and what logs we need from CypherTech. If we get Marta's artifacts early, we can do a dry-run on Mon evening.

Thanks everyone — looks like a tight but feasible schedule.

— Dev
Dev Patel | Staff Engineer, Redwood Inference
